research_rationale: Identity: the held Federal Register text (55 FR 33089, Monday, August 13, 1990, PDF pages 205-206) is Executive Order 12724 of August 9, 1990, blocking Government of Iraq property and prohibiting transactions with Iraq, with Sections 1 to 6 and no annex. The inventory of 17 clauses (Section 1; Section 2 and its lettered paragraphs including the (i)/(ii) fragment of 2(b); Section 3 and 3(a)-(b); Sections 4, 5 and 6) matches the text. Whole-order end: Executive Order 13350 of July 29, 2004 (69 FR 46055, Friday, July 30, 2004) revokes Executive Order 12724 of August 9, 1990 by name, as one of the orders based on the national emergency declared in Executive Order 12722, and section 10 provides that it is "effective at 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on July" 30, 2004. A search of the held corpus for the number 12724 found only Executive Order 13303 (May 22, 2003) and Executive Order 13350 as later orders naming it. Executive Order 13303 section 2(a) made Executive Orders 12722, 12724 and 13290 inapplicable only to the Iraqi petroleum and Development Fund for Iraq property described in its section 1; that is a partial narrowing and a later event on Section 1, not an end of any clause. No held source shows an earlier end of any other clause, so every clause ends with the revocation. Exclusive reading: the order is in force through 2004-07-29 and revoked from 12:01 a.m. on 2004-07-30. Current-law searches (U.S. Code and eCFR) were run by machine, found two hits each for this order, and are leads only; the order is NO so no current predicate is claimed.
savings_reason: Executive Order 13350 section 1 preserves pending actions and matured rights and penalties under section 202(a) of the National Emergencies Act, and determines under section 207(a) of IEEPA that the continuation of prohibitions on property blocked pursuant to Executive Orders 12722 or 12724 "that continues to be blocked as of the effective date of this order" is necessary on account of claims involving Iraq. The blocking of property already blocked therefore continued after the revocation under that determination, not under Executive Order 12724 itself, and is a residual of section 1 of this order. Executive Order 12724 section 6 likewise saved violations occurring while a provision of Executive Order 12722 was in effect. No clause of Executive Order 12724 itself continues operative after 2004-07-30. The machine current-law leads (31 CFR 576.201; note to 50 U.S.C. 1701) concern this continued blocking; their full texts are not held, so they are recorded as unread leads and not relied on.
conflict_resolutions: {"NO_ORDER_CITED_IN_CURRENT_LAW": "The machine current-law search names this order in the note headed Iraq Sanctions to 50 U.S.C. 1701 and in 31 CFR 576.201. Full legal-text slices of those provisions are not held (the packet records them as citation or pointer only), so they are read only as leads: the statutory note describes the sanctions imposed by the August 9, 1990 orders, and the regulation lead concerns property blocked under Executive Orders 12722 and 12724 that continued to be blocked on July 30, 2004. Both are consistent with the held Executive Order 13350, which revoked this order effective 12:01 a.m. on 2004-07-30 and in its section 1 determined under IEEPA section 207(a) that continued prohibitions on already-blocked property are necessary. That continuation is a savings residual resting on Executive Order 13350 and implementing regulations, not a surviving clause of Executive Order 12724, so the provisional status NO stands. A current-law mention is a lead and not a basis, and no held current-law text shows any clause of this order operating after the revocation."}
earlier_end_check: Searched held texts for the number 12724: only Executive Orders 13303 and 13350 name it. Executive Order 13303 section 2(a) is partial (property in its section 1 only) and is recorded as a later event on Section 1. Executive Order 13350 revokes the whole order. No held source shows regulations, licences or statutes extinguishing any other clause earlier; regulations and licences are contemplated by the order itself as exceptions, and so are not ends.
scope_check: All 17 clauses are inventoried from the held Federal Register text and each ends with the order as a whole on 2004-07-30. Definition and effective-date clauses (Sections 3 and 4) have no separate end beyond the revocation of the order.
independent_command_check: No command of this order rests on a separate authority that survived its revocation: Section 5 is a delegation within this order, and the post-revocation continuation of prohibitions on blocked property rests on the determination in Executive Order 13350 section 1, which is recorded as savings and not as a continuing clause.
savings_check: Savings are stated from Executive Order 13350 section 1 (National Emergencies Act section 202(a); IEEPA section 207(a)); no other savings clause bears on this order.
